newsitem.title: CHINA: Japan may give yen loans for Shanghai new airport.
newsitem.headline: Japan may give yen loans for Shanghai new airport.

text.p: Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Thursday Japan would decide as early as July on yen loans for the new Shanghai international airport that China has been requesting.

"We hope to decide on extending the yen loan as early as possible," Mitsuzuka told Shanghai mayor Xu Kuangdi, adding that the decision was unlikely by the end of this month, but may be possible in July.
Mitsuzuka is on a four-day visit to China and is due to return to Japan on Friday.

China has been requesting 16.5 billion yen worth of yen loans for a new international airport now under construction in the Pudong development zone. The airport is due to open in 2000 with a single runway and initial terminal capacity for 20 million passengers.
This is a part of the 580 billion yen in yen loans to China planned for the 1996-1998 fiscal year period by the Japanese government.
Mitsuzuka also told Xu that Japan would be happy to extend know-how for development of Shanghai's financial markets.
"I hope to deepen and continue economic cooperation with Shanghai," Mitsuzuka said.
